subject: Tenant environment commissioning: account prerequisites & egress flow
messages:
From: Alex Li <alex.li@medicore.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: ops+infra@medicore.com
Date: 2026-08-17T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Tenant environment commissioning & network walkthrough

Hi Logan,

Thanks for picking this up. We're kicking off the commissioning of a tenant VPC that will host our private Redwood deployment. Before we lock a call I'd like to confirm a few technical prerequisites so we can surface anything that affects our networking and procurement teams: 

- Outbound/egress destinations Redwood will contact (IPs/domains) and whether TLS inspection is supported on our side.
- Preferred NAT behavior: source NAT / 1:1 mapping / shared egress IP pools.
- Required TCP/UDP ports and any ephemeral ranges we need to allow.
- Recommended IP ranges your runtime might present (for firewall whitelist).
- Any BGP/ASN requirements or overlapping ASN guidance (we run BGP to our edge).
- TLS certificate expectations (SANs, rotation window) and whether Redwood supports customer-provided certs or uses mTLS to your control plane.
- KMS/HSM integration points for key wrapping or encryption-at-rest evidence.
- Telemetry/metrics ingestion endpoints and expected sampling volumes.
- Typical maintenance windows and transparent MTR/RTO targets for private deployments.

We can provide our network diagrams and firewall export if that helps — I'm attaching our initial export in the next message. Propose a 30-min tech sync next Tue/Wed (Aug 24/25) 10–12 PT.

Appreciate a compact checklist we can pass to our security and networking folks.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Li
Head of Infrastructure, Medicore
[Attachment: medicore_firewall_export_0817.csv (CSV, 85KB)]

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-08-17T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Tenant environment commissioning & network walkthrough

Alex — thanks, this is a great starting list. I've pulled together a compact technical checklist below that covers what we need for a smooth private deployment handoff. Marissa (Private Deployments) and Kim (Network Security) are cc'd to add specifics.

High-level checklist (what we need from Medicore for day 0):
1) Egress/allowlist
  - Fully qualified domains and IPs Redwood will contact: API endpoints (runtime + control plane), telemetry endpoints, license/usage checks. See attached redwood_network_template_v1.pdf for our canonical list — please fill and return.
2) Egress behavior
  - Preferred: SNAT to a small pool of egress IPs you control OR we can operate behind your NAT if you provide stable, routable egress addresses.
3) Ports
  - Outbound 443 to our control plane and telemetry; inbound only for admin bastion (SSH/443) on locked CIDRs.
4) BGP/ASN overlap
  - If you have overlapping RFC1918 subnets we prefer to NAT at the edge; for public ASN overlap we can coordinate a targeted route-map. If you can share your ASN and a brief routing table export it'll help.
5) TLS certs & mTLS
  - We support both: customer-supplied certs on ingress (you manage rotation) or Redwood-managed certs with a rotation policy (default 90 days). For control-plane calls we do TLS; mTLS can be enabled for telemetry if requested.
6) KMS integration
  - We can integrate with AWS KMS / GCP KMS / Azure Key Vault; please specify CMK ARNs or key IDs and the contact for key rotation policy.
7) Telemetry
  - Endpoint URLs and approximate qps/ingest. We prefer HTTPS with basic auth/token header.
8) Maintenance windows & SLOs
  - Proposed maintenance window: Sun 02:00–06:00 PT. We'll provide SLO targets by environment type once we see expected request volumes.

Attachments for your fill-in: redwood_network_template_v1.pdf (canonical allowlist + egress domains) and a blank mutual action plan.

Can you populate the template and share your firewall export? If the BGP/asn bit is sticky, we can do the initial deployment behind your NAT and revisit BGP peering later. Proposed sync: Wed Aug 25th 11:00 PT — works for you?

Best,
Logan Wright
Partnerships & Deployments, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_network_template_v1.pdf (PDF, 120KB)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Li <alex.li@medicore.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-17T14:08:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Tenant environment commissioning & network walkthrough

Alex — quick technical notes to help your networking/security teams. I'm pasting answers inline for the key items you listed.

On Tue, Aug 17, 2026 at 09:12 AM Alex Li <alex.li@medicore.com> wrote:
> - Outbound/egress destinations Redwood will contact (IPs/domains) and whether TLS inspection is supported on our side.

- See redwood_network_template_v1.pdf: primary domains are runtime.redwood.ai, control.redwood.ai, telemetry.redwood.ai. IPs are subject to change per region; prefer domain-based allowlisting. TLS inspection is OK for outgoing telemetry as long as agent headers are preserved (we send a small attestation header).

> - Preferred NAT behavior: source NAT / 1:1 mapping / shared egress IP pools.

- We recommend a small static pool (2–4 IPs) for egress if you want stable allowlist entries. Alternatively we can accept SNAT behind your NAT but we will need to validate source mapping during smoke.

> - Required TCP/UDP ports and any ephemeral ranges we need to allow.

- Outbound: 443 (all services). Inbound: 22 (bastion) — lock to jump-host CIDRs; 443 for admin panels if enabled. No UDP required for baseline deployment.

> - BGP/ASN requirements or overlapping ASN guidance

- If RFC1918 overlap exists, our recommended pattern: perform one-sided NAT at your edge for tenant subnets to avoid route leaks. For public ASN overlaps, we can coordinate specific route-maps and prepended routes. Please share ASN and route table snippet.

> - TLS certificate expectations (SANs, rotation window)

- For customer-supplied certs we require SANs listing the tenant FQDN(s). Rotation: we ask for a 30-day notification before expiry. We can also manage certs and provide auto-rotation.

> - KMS/HSM integration points

- We'll accept wrapped keys using your KMS; we require a service account with decrypt permissions scoped to the keys for initial key unwrap. For HSM-backed keys please share the connector type.

> - Telemetry endpoints and expected sampling volumes

- Telemetry ingestion endpoints accept TLS POSTs to telemetry.redwood.ai/api/v1/push. Start with sampling ~10qps per 100k requests — we'll validate after baseline traffic.

I've attached the redwood_network_template_v1.pdf for you to annotate and return. If you can also export a small & sanitized routing table that shows your public prefixes and any edge NAT ranges, that will help Kim and our network team.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Manager, Private Deployments — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_network_template_v1.pdf (PDF, 120KB)]
